text:
Predicates:
NamedAfter(x, y) ::: x is named after y.
GoodGuys(x) ::: x are good guys.
Win(x) ::: x wins.
Fight(x, y) ::: x fights y.
Nemesis(x, y) ::: x is the nemesis of y.
InMovie(x, y) ::: x is in the movie y.
Character(y) ::: y is a character.

Premises:
In superhero movies, the good guys always win ::: ∀x (Movie(x) → ∀y (GoodGuys(y) → Wins(y)))
The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is a superhero movie ::: Movie(surprising_adventures)
Good guys fight bad guys and vice versa ::: ∀x, y (Fight(x, y) → (GoodGuys(x) ∧ BadGuys(y) ∨ BadGuys(x) ∧ GoodGuys(y)))
Sir Digby fights his nemesis ::: Fight(sir_digby, nemesis)
If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character is a good guy ::: ∀x, y (NamedAfter(x, y) ∧ Movie(x) → GoodGuys(y))
The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is named after Sir Digby ::: NamedAfter(surprising_adventures, sir_digby)
If somebody wins a fight, the person they are fighting does not win ::: ∀x, y (Fight(x, y) ∧ Wins(x) → ¬Wins(y))
If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character is in the movie ::: ∀x, y (NamedAfter(x, y) ∧ Movie(x) → InMovie(y, x))
Character(sir_digby) ::: sir_digby is a character.

Conclusion:
¬Wins(nemesis) ::: Sir Digby's nemesis does not win.
